name: Bloc Projects
funding: Bloc Projects received £8600 from the National Lottery Heritage Fund in 2017 under its Sharing Heritage programme.

name: Site Gallery
funding: £565k income (FY2025). Arts Council England £320k, Sheffield City Council, Esmée Fairbairn, JG Graves, Jerwood, University of Sheffield, Fidelity UK Foundation; Foyle, Garfield Weston and Wolfson capital grants.

name: John Hansard Gallery
funding: The University of Southampton funds it. Arts Council England has funded it since its inception.

name: Coaxial Arts Foundation
funding: Grants and corporate underwriting come from California Arts Council, City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs and Andy Warhol Foundation For The Visual Arts Inc.

name: Human Resources LA (HRLA)
funding: The Andy Warhol Foundation, Los Angeles County Arts Commission, Mike Kelley Foundation, Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and Ruth Foundation for the Arts support it in part.

name: LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions)
funding: California Arts Council, Andy Warhol Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts, Mike Kelley Foundation. 501(c)(3) public non-profit returns.

name: REDCAT (Roy and Edna Disney/CalArts Theater)
funding: CalArts is its parent organization. The Walt Disney Company and the County of Los Angeles gave financial support when it opened in November 2003.

name: ABC No Rio
funding: The rebuild drew on capital funding from the city's cultural affairs department. The organization has raised $21 million.

name: American Folk Art Museum
funding: Members support the exhibitions and educational programs. The Institute of Museum and Library Services funded at least one project.

name: Apexart
funding: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts supports its exhibitions and public programs in part.

name: Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM)
funding: In fiscal year 2025 BAM took $34,598,481 in contributions and $16,799,670 in program service revenue, of $52,530,452 total revenue.

name: CUE Art Foundation
funding: National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), NYSCA, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, private philanthropic grants. 501(c)(3) public non-profit.
